history.summary: IDENTITY PROVISIONAL (verify): the CSV name 'Sri Radha Krishna Mandir, Bhopal' is generic — Bhopal has several temples of this name (Punjabi Bagh, Kolar Road, Old Ashoka Garden, and the main ISKCON Bhopal at Raisen Road/Patel Nagar). This file provisionally documents the centre listed as 'Sri Sri Radha Krishna Mandir BHEL' (indiainfo.net / worldorgs), i.e. ISKCON BHEL-Bhopal, officially the 'Sri Sri Radha Govind Dev Temple' at Hare Krishna Land, Sector A, Berkheda, Bhopal 462022. It is a branch of ISKCON (founded 1966 by A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada), established in 2020, focused on congregation and youth preaching in Bhopal colleges, with a weekly Sunday feast, kirtan, Gita classes and prasadam distribution (2000+ people weekly, per the centre's listing). MEDIA EMPTY: no verifiable image of this specific centre found after genuine searching — do not substitute an image of another Bhopal ISKCON centre.

town_description: Bhopal, the capital of Madhya Pradesh, is known as the 'City of Lakes' for its twin Upper and Lower Lakes, the larger Upper Lake (Bhojtal) attributed to the 11th-century Paramara king Raja Bhoja. The city blends historic Islamic-era architecture — the Begums of Bhopal ruled here for over a century — with modern institutions, museums and a fast-growing new city. It is the state's administrative and cultural hub, well connected by rail, air and road, and a gateway to heritage sites like Sanchi, Bhimbetka and Bhojpur.
